# The Central Limit Theorem {#sec-interactive-clt}

The app below runs entirely in your browser using WebAssembly (Python via
Pyodide, built with [marimo](https://marimo.io)). Choose a population and a
sample size, and watch the distribution of sample means become bell-shaped.

::: {.column-page}
```{=html}
<iframe src="../apps/clt_demo/index.html"
        title="Central Limit Theorem explorer"
        style="width:100%; height:720px; border:1px solid #ccc; border-radius:6px;"
        loading="lazy"></iframe>
```
:::

[Open the app in its own tab](../apps/clt_demo/index.html){target="_blank"}

::: {.callout-note}
The first load downloads the Python runtime (~10–20 MB) and may take a few
seconds; later visits are cached by the browser.
:::

## Things to try

1. Start with the *Exponential* population and $n = 1$. What shape do you see?
2. Increase $n$ to 5, 10, 30. When does the histogram look roughly normal?
3. Repeat with the *Bernoulli(0.2)* population. Does it need a larger $n$?
